# EDC — Architecture Overview

EDC packages deep codebase-context generation and context-aware review across multiple agent runtimes. The repo's behavior is split between shell control-plane scripts, plugin/hook surfaces, canonical prompt/skill files, thin agent wrappers, a benchmark/autoresearch harness, and hardening tests that lock down the runtime contract.

## Module Map

| Module | Purpose | Deep Context | Representative Files |
|---|---|---|---|
| `runtime-cli` | Public shell entrypoints, install routing, review orchestration, ignore handling, timeout/content validation | `.context/runtime-cli.md` | `scripts/edc`, `scripts/edc-review.sh`, `install.sh` |
| `plugin-surface` | Claude plugin packaging, slash-command adapters, session-start and pre-edit context injection | `.context/plugin-surface.md` | `plugins/edc/commands/*`, `plugins/edc/hooks/*` |
| `canonical-skills` | Single-source prompt corpus for build/update/split/audit/review behavior | `.context/canonical-skills.md` | `plugins/edc/skills/*` |
| `agent-wrappers` | Cursor/Codex/Gemini installers and thin runtime-specific wrappers/docs | `.context/agent-wrappers.md` | `agents/cursor/**`, `agents/codex/**`, `agents/gemini/**` |
| `benchmarking` | CVE benchmark runner, scorer, prompt-tuning loop, ground-truth corpus | `.context/benchmarking.md` | `benchmark/run.sh`, `benchmark/autoresearch.sh`, `benchmark/score.py` |
| `hardening-tests` | Executable compatibility contract for runtime/orchestrator behavior | `.context/hardening-tests.md` | `tests/hardening/*.sh` |

## Actors

- Human users invoking build/review/install flows.
- Agent CLIs: Claude, Cursor, Codex, and partially Gemini.
- Plugin/hook runtime that injects `.context/` files into sessions.
- External binaries: `git`, `jq`, `gh`, `node`, `python3`, `curl`, `timeout/gtimeout`.
- Benchmark harness operating on hostile third-party repos/CVE revisions.

## Key Flows

- Install: copy canonical prompt/runtime assets into agent-specific homes and `.edc/scripts/`.
- Build context: `scripts/edc build` -> agent-specific prompt resolution -> `edc-build-impl` -> `.context/full-context.md` -> split outputs -> complexity audit.
- Review: `scripts/edc review` / plugin wrapper -> orchestrator -> missing/stale context recovery -> `review-tasks/` -> per-module subprocess review -> `review-*.md`.
- Session injection: session-start injects overview context; pre-tool hook injects one relevant module file per session.
- Benchmark/autoresearch: mutate review prompt corpus, score against curated CVE sets, keep only improvements that survive regression checks.

## Global Invariants

- `.context/.meta.json:lastCommit` must equal current `HEAD` for context to be considered fresh.
- `.context/context.md` and `review-tasks/report-*.md` must contain `##` headings; structureless output is treated as failure.
- Runtime review selection must exclude `.context/`, `review-tasks/`, and `review-*.md` to avoid self-review.
- Cursor/Codex wrappers are thin shells over canonical `plugins/edc/skills/*` content.
- Hardening tests are the practical specification for shell/orchestrator behavior.
- Hooks depend on `modules -> files -> contextFile` mappings in `.context/.meta.json`.

## Trust Boundaries

- User arguments, PR URLs, diff files, and `.edcignore` patterns are untrusted input.
- Skill markdown and command markdown are executable control data for subprocess agents.
- Hook input schemas differ across Claude/Cursor and are normalized defensively.
- External repos and vulnerable revisions in `benchmark/` are hostile input.

## Cascade-Risk Coupling

- Renaming skill directories or command files breaks runtime prompt resolution, installers, and hardening tests together.
- Changing `.meta.json` shape breaks hooks, update flows, and context freshness checks.
- Adjusting orchestrator flags/output affects three surfaces at once: runtime shell, mocked tests, and benchmark/autoresearch subprocess handling.
- Duplicate file manifests across installers create intentional loud-failure behavior, but also raise drift risk.

# EDC Architecture Overview

EDC is a multi-runtime toolkit for two linked jobs: build deep architectural context for a repo, then use that context to drive structured differential review. The implementation is shell-first and file-backed: wrappers launch agent runtimes, the orchestrator manages review state in `.context/` and `review-tasks/`, and Node hooks inject just enough context back into active sessions.

The codebase is organized around a small set of runtime-critical modules plus a large prompt-asset layer. `scripts/edc` is the thin terminal entrypoint, `plugins/edc/scripts/edc-review.sh` is the heavy control plane, `plugins/edc/hooks/*.mjs` make context injection ergonomic, and the remaining installer/wrapper files package the same workflow for Claude, Cursor, Codex, and Gemini.

## Modules

| Module | Purpose | Key Files | Deep Context |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cli-wrapper` | Terminal build/review entrypoint | `scripts/edc`, `README.md` | `.context/cli-wrapper.md` |
| `plugin-interface` | Claude plugin commands, metadata, hook registration | `plugins/edc/commands/*`, `plugins/edc/.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `plugins/edc/hooks/hooks.json` | `.context/plugin-interface.md` |
| `review-orchestrator` | Context gate, task generation, subprocess review pipeline | `plugins/edc/scripts/edc-review.sh`, `scripts/edc-review.sh`, `.edc/scripts/edc-review.sh` | `.context/review-orchestrator.md` |
| `hook-runtime` | Session-start and pre-tool context injection | `plugins/edc/hooks/session-start.mjs`, `plugins/edc/hooks/pretooluse-context-inject.mjs` | `.context/hook-runtime.md` |
| `build-review-skills` | Shared prompt assets for build, update, split, audit, review | `plugins/edc/skills/**` | `.context/build-review-skills.md` |
| `agent-installers` | Per-agent installers, wrapper commands/skills, docs | `install.sh`, `agents/**` | `.context/agent-installers.md` |
| `hardening-tests` | Shell smoke tests that pin workflow contracts | `tests/hardening/*.sh` | `.context/hardening-tests.md` |

## Actors

- Developer using Claude, Cursor, Codex, Gemini, or the terminal.
- Agent runtime CLIs that consume prompts and write artifacts.
- `git` and `gh`, which define scope and freshness.
- Node hook scripts that inject context into live sessions.
- The filesystem under `.context/`, `.edc/scripts/`, and `review-tasks/`, which acts as the workflow state store.

## Key Flows

- Build: wrapper/command -> `edc-build-impl` -> full context or incremental update -> `.context/*`.
- Review: runtime wrapper -> `.edc/scripts/edc-review.sh` -> freshness gate -> build/update if needed -> per-module review tasks -> consolidated `review-*.md`.
- Session injection: `SessionStart` reads `.context/context.md`; `PreToolUse` resolves edited files to modules and injects only the matching `.context/{module}.md`.

## Global Invariants

- `.context/.meta.json:lastCommit` must equal `git rev-parse HEAD` before review can proceed.
- `.context/context.md` and each review report must contain at least one `##` heading or they are treated as invalid/stub output.
- Runtime wrappers stay thin and defer actual behavior to the shared skills or orchestrator.
- Installer file lists must remain synchronized across remote and local install paths.
- Hook module injection only works when `.context/.meta.json.modules` accurately maps source files to module files.

## Trust Boundaries

- User-supplied review targets, paths, ignore globs, and PR URLs.
- Agent subprocess output before structural validation.
- Git/GitHub diff data used to decide review scope.
- Project-local `.edc/scripts/edc-review.sh`, which can drift from the plugin-bundled script.
- Hook payload JSON and Bash command parsing in `pretooluse-context-inject.mjs`.

## Coupling / Cascade Risk

- Renaming skill directories or wrapper filenames forces changes across installers, docs, wrappers, and tests.
- Changing orchestrator flags or output paths breaks runtime wrappers and multiple hardening tests together.
- A stale or divergent project-local orchestrator copy can put docs, tests, and real execution on different code paths.
